capabilities: Run code blocks in Obsidian across Python, Julia, R, JavaScript, TypeScript, Bash, Rust and other Jupyter kernels
Capture rich outputs such as plots, images, dataframes and magic commands below each code block
Convert Markdown notes into .ipynb notebooks and .ipynb notebooks into Markdown notes
Sync changes bidirectionally between paired .md and .ipynb files, including output metadata
Keep variables and imports from earlier code blocks available in later ones
extras: Desktop-only plugin; requires a local Python tooling environment, which can be set up from the plugin settings. The README includes a security section noting that executed code runs with Obsidian's operating-system permissions and warns to only run trusted notebooks. No telemetry or network requests, except user-confirmed package installs.
problem: Obsidian has no way to execute code blocks or treat Markdown notes as runnable Jupyter notebooks with persistent outputs.

relations.evidence: Python is necessary as a tooling environment to invoke Jupytext and Jupyter Client

requires.name: Python with Jupytext and Jupyter Client (plus language kernels for non-Python languages)
